title: Scripture and Prayer
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Scripture and prayer teaches that God’s Word shapes the way believers pray, and prayer opens the heart to receive God’s Word with faith. Scripture teaches believers how to worship, confess, ask, thank, lament, and trust before God.
summary: Scripture and prayer teaches that God’s Word shapes the way believers pray, and prayer opens the heart to receive God’s Word with faith. Scripture teaches believers how to worship, confess, ask, thank, lament, and trust before God.
christFocus: Jesus’ words abide in His people and shape their prayers. Through Scripture, believers learn to pray in the name of Christ, according to God’s will, with dependence on the Father and help from the Holy Spirit.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Scripture and prayer belong together. God speaks through His Word, and His people answer Him in prayer. The Word gives prayer truth, depth, reverence, confession, promise, and direction.

Jesus taught that if His words abide in His disciples, their prayers will be shaped by His will. Prayer is not a way to bend God to human desires, but a means of living in dependent communion with Him.

Scripture gives believers language for every season. The Psalms teach worship, lament, confession, thanksgiving, fear, longing, hope, and trust. The prayers of Scripture train believers to come honestly and reverently before God.

Prayer also seeks help to receive and obey the Word. Believers ask God to give understanding, revive the soul, strengthen faith, and make His Word fruitful in them.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Prayer can become shallow when separated from Scripture, and Bible reading can become cold when separated from prayer. Some pray only from emotion, while others study without dependence. God invites His people into both truth and communion.

This doctrine is especially helpful for those who do not know what to pray. Scripture gives words when the heart feels empty, confused, grieving, fearful, or ashamed. God’s Word teaches believers how to come near.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Let Scripture shape your prayers. Pray God’s promises, confess sins Scripture exposes, ask for help to obey what God commands, and turn biblical truth into worship. When you open the Bible, ask God to teach you; when you pray, let His Word guide your heart toward Christ.
